newsitem.title: HUNGARY: LOCKHEED SEEKS F-16 OFFSET DEAL WITH HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: LOCKHEED SEEKS F-16 OFFSET DEAL WITH HUNGARY.

text.p: U.S.'s Lockheed Martin Corp. said it would invest in Hungary an equal amount to the purchase price of its F-16s, should the country opt for their fighters.
"We would offer Hungary a 100 percent offset deal," Dain Hancock, President of Lockheed's tactical aircraft systems, told a news conference, but said the details would be worked out later.
He also confirmed that the fly-away purchase price of an F-16 is $24 million, but the actual price would depend on the size of the order.

Lockheed Martin is competing for post-Cold War business in central Europe against U.S. McDonnell Douglas , maker of the F-18 "Hornet", Sweden's SAAB, which makes the "Gripen", France's "Mirage" and other European builders.
Hungary has an air wing of 28 MiG-29s that would be operational well into the next century, but its older MiG-21, MiG-23 and Su-22 airplanes need replacement.
Defence ministry sources said Hungary - depending on the timescale of NATO membership - is looking to buy some 30 fighters.
